props.gloss_en: the slaughterer needs three knives: one to slaughter with, one to cut meat, one to cut forbidden fats
[one knife for meat-then-fats is not allowed:] a decree, lest he cut fats and then meat
the slaughterer needs two vessels of water: one to rinse meat, one to rinse forbidden fats
[one vessel for meat-then-fats is not allowed:] a decree, lest he rinse fats and then meat
a person should not lay the flanks over meat
because the forbidden fat flows and the meat absorbs it
[flanks in their usual position are fine:] the membrane interposes from below
a Torah scholar must learn writing
a Torah scholar must learn slaughter
a Torah scholar must learn circumcision
also the knot of the tefillin
and the grooms' blessing
and tzitzit
and the other [tradition omits them because] those are common
any slaughterer who does not know the halakhot of slaughter -- one may not eat from his slaughter
and these are the halakhot of slaughter: pausing, pressing, concealing, diverting, and ripping
the dictum is needed for one who slaughtered well before us two or three times: since he did not learn, sometimes he pauses or presses and does not know it
the slaughterer must examine the simanim after slaughter
R' Shimon: [the slaughter is invalid] if he paused the length of an examination
R' Yochanan: [R' Shimon's measure is] the length of an examination by a sage
rather: the length of an examination by a slaughterer who is a sage
[if he did not examine the simanim:] it is tereifa and forbidden to eat
[if he did not examine the simanim:] it is nevela and imparts impurity by carrying
it stands in its presumption of prohibition, and now it is dead [so it is nevela]
a presumption of prohibition we say; a presumption of impurity we do not say
an animal in its life stands in a presumption of prohibition until you know how it was slaughtered
once slaughtered, it stands in a presumption of permission until you know how it became tereifa
[the wording 'stands in a presumption of permission' teaches:] even if a flaw arose in it, the presumption stands
[innards a wolf took and returned perforated:] we do not suspect that it perforated at the place of a perforation
one who saw a bird pecking a fig or a mouse gnawing melons -- we suspect it pecked at the place of a perforation
danger is different from (more severe than) prohibition
Rava: what is different? a doubt of danger is ruled stringently, and a doubt of prohibition is ruled stringently too
a doubt of impurity in the public domain -- it is pure
a doubt whether water was left exposed -- it is forbidden
there it is a halakha learned from sota: as sota is in the private domain, so impurity [of doubt] is in the private domain
a creeping thing in a weasel's mouth, the weasel walking on teruma loaves, doubt whether it touched -- it is pure
there too it is learned from sota: as sota is a thing with understanding to be asked, so here [only] a thing with understanding to be asked
a flask he left uncovered and found covered is impure, for I say: an impure man entered and covered it
left covered and found uncovered: if a weasel could drink from it, or dew fell in it at night -- it is disqualified
or [if] a snake [could drink from it], according to Rabban Gamliel
R' Yehoshua b. Levi: what is the reason [found uncovered is not impure]? because creeping things' way is to uncover, not to cover
but found as he left it -- there is neither impurity nor disqualification
three liquids are forbidden on account of exposure: water, wine and milk
how long until they are forbidden? long enough for a snake to come out from a near place and drink
Rav Yitzchak b. Rav Yehuda: a near place is enough to come out from under the vessel's handle and drink
rather: [long enough to come out,] drink, and return to its hole
